videos.title: Trump Says He May Become ‘Mr. Veto’ if Democrats Win Midterms
videos.description:
President Trump says he may have to become "Mr. Veto" if Democrats win a majority in tomorrow's midterms, a rare acknowledgement that Republicans could lose the elections. With one day to go, polls suggest Democrats could make gains in the House and Senate as they seek control of both chambers of Congress.

US equity futures advanced to halt a bruising selloff in the artificial intelligence trade, with falling oil prices helping stocks to start the month on a positive note.

Apple reports earnings after the bell on Monday. The iPhone maker's stock has climbed 25% from a low in late June, adding roughly $1 trillion in market value, as the company’s steady revenue growth and rising free cash flow have offered a haven for investors balked by concerns about heavy spending on AI infrastructure by megacap peers like Alphabet and Amazon.

Today's guests: Derek Halpenny, MUFG Head of Research for Global Markets; Jeff Currie, Real Macro CEO; Tina Fordham, Fordham Global Foresight Founder

videos.title: Hormuz Reopening Talks Advance as Iran Warns of Wider Response if Attacked
videos.description:
Oil slips as hopes for Iran diplomacy improve. Tehran says Hormuz talks remain on track and has floated a two-day reopening plan, while Gulf states continue pushing for a deal. Iran also warns it is prepared for a broader response if attacked.
US midterm politics remain in focus, with Trump saying he could become “Mr. Veto” if Democrats win. Early voting shows stronger Democratic turnout, while Republicans face pressure from Trump’s approval ratings and Democrats continue to wrestle with internal divisions.
In the UAE, OpenAI signs new agreements with local companies as Sam Altman meets Abu Dhabi’s crown prince. Aramco also closes a $2.6 billion deal with Saudi PIF to acquire a stake in Humain.
Paul Donovan of UBS says long-term structural trends matter more than short-term volatility and sees shifting global capital flows supporting the UAE. Oaktree’s Howard Marks says the current AI cycle is unlike anything he has seen.
Technology remains active: OpenAI reportedly cuts its latest fundraising target by $10 billion, DeepSeek launches a coding agent aimed at Anthropic, and Foxconn says AI demand remains exceptionally strong.
Binance reports $3.6 billion in outflows following the cyber theft, while the FBI blames North Korea for the wider $6 billion hack.
Elsewhere, protests in Germany focus on affordability, Indians rally over voter-roll changes, OPay pauses its IPO amid regulatory questions, South Africa awaits a US decision on AGOA eligibility, Russia halts recruitment of Ghanaians for the Ukraine war, and a Kenyan tribunal dismisses a case linked to Dangote’s refinery. Guests include Paul Donovan, UBS Global Wealth Management Chief Economist.

Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.

videos.title: What’s the risk of political violence? | Martin Wolf on the US midterms | FT
videos.description:
As Americans prepare to vote in the November 3 midterm elections, the FT’s chief economics commentator Martin Wolf asks what the result will mean for Donald Trump, the future of US democracy and America's place in the world. 

In the third of a six-part series, Martin speaks to political scientist and author Barbara F Walter, an expert on civil wars and political violence, about the risk of unrest surrounding the elections. 

Drawing on her research into countries around the world, Walter explains the warning signs of political violence, and why America's changing demographics and the struggle to hold on to political power are fuelling divisions. How close is the US to a dangerous tipping point? And can American democracy emerge from the midterms stronger rather than more divided?

To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts.

videos.title: The 'Socialist' Bank Thriving In Trump Country
videos.description:
Progressive political candidates have clamored to launch public banks in the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections. However, there is just one active example in the United States: the Bank of North Dakota. Chartered in 1919, this bank uses tax revenue from the state to fund and execute strategic economic development priorities for North Dakota. The bank has assisted in sales of fossil fuel assets, a presidential library, and general lending to citizens and businesses in need. CNBC's Garrett Downs reports on this “socialist experiment” unfolding deep in Trump country.

videos.title: Ajay Banga on AI, Jobs & Opportunity | Global AI & Digital Summit
videos.description:
At the Global AI & Digital Summit in Seoul, World Bank Group President Ajay Banga discusses the future of development, the role of digital technology, and the opportunities and challenges presented by artificial intelligence.

He discusses the importance of getting the fundamentals of digital development right, including electricity, connectivity, affordability and digital public infrastructure, and shares examples of how locally relevant AI tools are being used in agriculture, health and education.

videos.title: The Race To Power AI Is Reshaping America's Electric Grid
videos.description:
AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting renewed pressure on America’s power grid to modernize its equipment and develop greener, more efficient sources of power. Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon are all spending millions of dollars on local infrastructure upgrades and companies like SpaceXAI are even building off-grid power plants to power their data centers.

Google says its planned 780-megawatt data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google says it will support 1,900 megawatts of new wind, solar and battery capacity, while minimum payments and exit fees are intended to protect local ratepayers if demand falls short.

CNBC examines whether projects like Pine Island can make the grid cleaner without shifting costs to existing customers, why some energy experts argue that smaller data centers could make better use of infrastructure already in place, and how utilities’ financial incentives can complicate efforts to build less.

videos.title: Why Fuel Economy Rollbacks Will Spur More Trucks, More V-8 Engines
videos.description:
Lowered compliance costs, greater control over products, more big engines, more pickup trucks. These are just some of the changes investors expect from the rollback of fuel economy rules and the elimination of fines. Data indicate pent up demand for pickup trucks, and many automakers are bringing back V-8 engines. At the same time, hybrid vehicles are surging, and electric vehicles have longer term structural demand in their favor.

videos.title: Why More Americans Regret College And Homeownership
videos.description:
For generations, mortgages and student loans have been held up as textbook examples of “good debt,".This borrowing promises to  build wealth or increase your earning power over time. On the other side of the coin is so-called “bad debt”, things like auto loans or credit card debt that don’t provide a financial return over time. As the costs of buying a home and getting a degree have continued to climb, more Americans are questioning whether those “good debt” investments are actually paying off.
